title: Boats to Save People
statement:
A cleanup crew has to carry `n` pieces of waste to a collection point. Each piece weighs between `1.01` and `3.00` kg, given with exactly two decimal places. A piece cannot be split.

The crew packs the waste into bags. A bag can hold **any number of pieces** as long as their total weight is at most `3.00` kg.

Find the **minimum number of bags** needed to carry all the pieces.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` weights, each written with two decimal places (for example `1.30`).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of bags.
constraints: 1.01 ≤ weight ≤ 3.00, with exactly two decimal places

examples.explanation: Pair 1.30 with 1.60 (2.90 kg) and 1.40 with 1.50 (2.90 kg). Two bags are enough, and one bag cannot hold all four.
Only 1.40 and 1.50 fit together (2.90 kg). 1.70 cannot share a bag with anything, because 1.70 + 1.50 = 3.20 kg is too heavy. That leaves bags {1.40, 1.50}, {1.50}, {1.70}.
3.00 fills a bag on its own. 1.01 + 1.99 = 3.00 kg exactly, so they share the second bag.

hints: Every piece weighs more than 1 kg, so three pieces always exceed 3.00 kg. How many pieces can a bag hold at most?
Work in whole hundredths of a kilogram to avoid floating-point comparison problems, then sort the weights.
Take the heaviest unpacked piece. Try to put the lightest unpacked piece with it. If they do not fit, the heavy piece goes alone.
